definitions.explanation: A state where a place, vehicle, or event has reached its maximum capacity of people.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}が{満員|まんいん}で{乗|の}れなかった。
examples.english: The train was so packed I couldn't get on.

examples.japanese: コンサートは{満員|まんいん}{御礼|おんれい}だった。
examples.english: The concert was sold out (packed to capacity).

examples.japanese: {満員|まんいん}バスで{通勤|つうきん}するのは{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: Commuting on a packed bus is tough.

notes:
WORD STRUCTURE:
{満|まん} (full) + {員|いん} (member, person)
Literally: "full of members/people"

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{満員|まんいん}{電車|でんしゃ} - packed train
・{満員|まんいん}バス - packed bus
・{満員|まんいん}{御礼|おんれい} - sold out (theatrical expression, lit. "thanks for the full house")
・{満員|まんいん}になる - to become full

RELATED WORDS:
・{満席|まんせき} - fully booked (seats)
・{空席|くうせき} - empty seat, vacancy
・{定員|ていいん} - capacity, fixed number
・すし{詰|づ}め - packed like sardines

CULTURAL NOTE:
{満員|まんいん}{電車|でんしゃ} (packed trains) are a well-known feature of Japanese urban life, especially during rush hours in Tokyo and other major cities.
